updates.name: Tilden P. Meyers
updates.bio: Senior scientist at NOAA's Air Resources Laboratory and its liaison to NOAA's Earth System Research Laboratories since 2009. He studies land-surface energy and carbon exchange, both by measurement and modeling, aiming to better represent the surface and boundary layer. Previously deputy and acting director of ARL's Atmospheric Turbulence and Diffusion Division; Purdue PhD in micrometeorology.
updates.research_interests: measurement and modeling of land-surface energy and carbon fluxes; land surface-boundary layer flux interactions; surface and boundary-layer representation in weather and climate models
updates.current_title: Senior Scientist, ARL Liaison to NOAA/ESRL

updates.name: Timothy J. Arkebauer
updates.bio: Professor emeritus in Agronomy and Horticulture at the University of Nebraska-Lincoln, working in crop and environmental physiology. His projects covered plant photoprotection under stress, scaling leaf responses up to canopies, soil trace-gas fluxes and soil carbon sequestration, and remote sensing of maize productivity. Nebraska PhD in agronomy (1986).
updates.research_interests: plant photoprotective mechanisms; leaf and canopy gas exchange; plant water relations; soil-plant-atmosphere relationships; soil surface trace gas fluxes; soil carbon sequestration
updates.notes: Status 'retired' rests on the emeritus title on the department profile. ORCID record 0000-0002-9731-7551 shows his name but no employment, so it is not adopted under the strict rule. | Verifier 2026-10-22: the profile returned 200 today and shows 'Professor Emeritus', 'Ph.D., Agronomy, University of Nebraska, 1986', and the research interests and project activities as paraphrased. The maize remote-sensing clause rests on the profile's listed publications. Kept.
updates.evidence: Timothy J. Arkebauer Professor Emeritus Agronomy & Horticulture University of Nebraska-Lincoln

updates.name: Tom Ford
updates.bio: Chief Executive Officer of The Bay Foundation, which he heads alongside directing the Santa Monica Bay National Estuary Program; also co-executive director of Loyola Marymount University's Coastal Research Institute, where he teaches environmental science. A marine ecologist (UCLA MA), he has worked on kelp forest restoration in Los Angeles since 1998.
updates.research_interests: kelp forest restoration; Marine Protected Area biological monitoring; abalone restoration and genetics; coastal climate vulnerability and resilience; ocean acidification and hypoxia; harmful algal blooms; eelgrass restoration

updates.name: Trevor F. Keenan
updates.bio: Professor in Environmental Science, Policy and Management at UC Berkeley who also leads a group affiliated with Berkeley Lab's Climate and Ecosystem Sciences Division. He investigates how land ecosystems respond to climate variability and change and feed back on the atmosphere via carbon and water cycling, blending eddy-covariance and satellite data with models and data assimilation.
updates.research_interests: ecosystem dynamics; carbon and water cycling; ecophysiology; vegetation states, rates and traits; biogeochemistry; micrometeorology; eddy-covariance and remote sensing data; data assimilation
updates.current_affiliation: University of California, Berkeley; Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory

updates.name: Walt Meier
updates.bio: Senior research scientist at the National Snow and Ice Data Center (CIRES, University of Colorado Boulder) and DAAC scientist for NASA's Snow and Ice DAAC. He studies sea ice using passive microwave remote sensing and tracks Arctic change, leads NASA's Arctic Sea Ice News and Analysis, and authors the sea ice chapter of NOAA's Arctic Report Card.
updates.research_interests: sea ice remote sensing; passive microwave sea ice data; Arctic sea ice and climate change monitoring; Arctic Sea Ice News and Analysis; NASA Snow and Ice DAAC data products
updates.current_affiliation: National Snow and Ice Data Center, CIRES, University of Colorado Boulder
